judgments.reasoning_cat1: The whereas clauses are aspirational recitals using broad language ('greatest benefits', 'most efficient service') that is not operative and hard to apply as a standard. Nothing in them creates a duty whose wording would itself need parsing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Recitals of this kind are routinely invoked to widen or narrow operative grants such as Section 1.2(g) ('project') and Section 3.8, so a recital-versus-operative-text argument is plausible here. Nothing directly contradicts them, however.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short-title provision with a single definite instruction; the only oddity is the duplicated period after 'title'. No term bears two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits consistently with Section 1.2(c), which defines 'Compact' as Part I of the act, and with the Part II state enactments. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The saving phrase 'except as may be otherwise required by the context' invites argument that a defined term does not govern in a given place, which is a genuine (if familiar) flexibility. Otherwise the introduction is mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That escape hatch bears directly on how the litigated definitions in 1.2(e) and 1.2(g) apply in Sections 3.8 and 11.2, so it could be pressed in aid of either reading. No outright inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Area of drainage into the Delaware River and its tributaries, including Delaware Bay' is a definite hydrological boundary; the only softness is where the Bay ends. No competing meanings are evident.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.7 (jurisdiction within the limits of the basin) and Article 10. No conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure naming definition tied to Section 2.1; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section 2.1's creation of the body politic exactly. Consistent with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: 'Compact' means Part I of this act. The word 'act' is used loosely across Part I and Part II but the definition itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.21 speaks of 'this Act' and of the Compact interchangeably, a slight looseness, but no operative contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Net induced adverse effects, whether or not compensated for' is a vague economic concept whose boundary cannot readily be fixed. That phrase is a real candidate for competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Sections 11.4 and 12.2 on cost allocation, which do not further define it, but nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition piles enumerated specifics onto 'any and all things and appurtenances necessary, useful or convenient' and closes with 'to facilitate any other uses of any of them', a classic general-versus-specific catch-all. The reach of that residual language is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Facility' is embedded in the definition of 'project' in 1.2(g) and thus in the Section 3.8 approval requirement, so its breadth was part of the same interpretive battleground. That interlock creates real whole-instrument tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any appropriate branch, department, bureau or division thereof, as the case may be' leaves 'appropriate' undefined, a mild vagueness. The core meaning is nevertheless plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 11.1 and the Part II federal reservations, which speak of particular federal agencies. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any work, service or activity which is separately planned, financed, or identified by the commission, or any separate facility ... for the conservation, utilization, control, development or management of water resources' is a sprawling, self-referential formula whose outer limit is genuinely contestable. This is precisely the kind of term two parties can read oppositely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reach determines the scope of Section 3.8's approval requirement and of Sections 11.1(b) and 11.2(b), and it must be squared with the narrower purposes recited in the preamble and Section 1.3; harmonising these leaves real uncertainty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, closed definition naming the states and the federal government. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its inclusion of the federal government within 'signatory party' does interact awkwardly with Section 12.8's exemption from 'taxation by ... any of the signatory parties', but the definition itself is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Related natural resources ... including related uses of land' is broad and open-textured; 'related' does much undefined work. That breadth is arguable but the drafters plainly intended width.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expands what falls under Article 6 flood plain and Article 7 watershed powers and interacts with Section 14.19's preservation of riparian law. No square conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introductory phrase; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Article 1 as a whole. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A declaratory finding rather than an operative obligation; 'affected with a local, state, regional and national interest' is general but not asked to do dispositive work. Little to parse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Findings like this are commonly deployed to colour the scope of Sections 3.6 and 3.8, so a purpose-versus-text argument is conceivable. No contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Joint exercise of such powers of sovereignty' is abstract but declaratory; no term carries two operative meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Sections 5.5, 11.3 and 14.19 reserving state authority, which pull the other way in emphasis but not in terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A single administrative agency is therefore essential' is a finding, definite in expression though hortatory in effect. Nothing ambiguous is named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Section 1.5's preservation of existing agencies and Sections 7.4(b)/8.2(b) preferring other operators, a difference in emphasis that could be argued as incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The finding that resources 'are ample to meet all presently projected demands' is a factual prediction that may be falsified, and the sentence runs two ideas together without punctuation. Mildly loose but not operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An aggrieved party could set this recital against the shortage machinery of Sections 10.2 and 10.4, which assume scarcity. That is a genuine, if soft, recital-versus-text tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of purposes ending in 'equal and uniform treatment to all water users who are similarly situated' — 'similarly situated' is vague, though the clause is declaratory. Some room to argue.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This purposes clause is the natural resource for construing the breadth of the Section 1.2(g) definition and Section 3.8, and its 'make secure and protect present developments' language can be urged against expansive regulation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard non-derogation clause with definite subject matter (navigable waters, commerce power). Little internal ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the express hook for the Part II reservations in Section 15.1 and for 15.1(t)'s exit mechanism; those provisions elaborate rather than contradict it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the fullest extent it finds feasible and advantageous' commits the question to the commission's own judgment, making the obligation nearly unmeasurable despite the word 'directed'. That is a genuine vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 7.4(b) and 8.2(b) expressly invoke this section's 'intent and purpose', while Section 1.3(c) declares a single agency essential; the pull in opposite directions is arguable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The renewal condition reads 'not later than 20 years nor sooner than 25 years prior to the termination', which is arithmetically inverted and cannot be performed as written — a mechanical error that changes the operative window.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the compact fixes the notice window, so the defect is internal to this provision rather than a clash with another clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in structure, though it leaves winding-up 'in such manner as may be provided by act of the Congress' with no default. A gap rather than an ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.1's 'succession for the duration of this compact' and with Section 1.4's recognition of congressional power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Creates the commission in definite terms as a body politic and corporate. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.1's corporate powers and with 15.1(m)'s statement that it is not a federal agency for certain statutes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The membership formula is plain on its face; 'to serve during the term of office of the President' is a definite tenure statement. No ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The compact's own endnote records that Sections 2.2 and 15.1(d) 'were inconsistent as to the term of the federal representative's appointment', an admitted internal conflict later cured by statute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The appointment, tenure and vacancy mechanics are stated definitely, with 'unless otherwise provided by law of the signatory party' as a clear override. Little to argue.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(d) makes the federal alternate serve at the President's pleasure, and New York §631 substitutes a further alternate, so the tenure rule here is qualified from outside.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Serve without compensation but may be reimbursed for necessary expenses' is definite, with only 'necessary' left soft. Low risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(r) expressly provides that notwithstanding Section 2.4 the federal member may be paid by the United States — a reconciled but real departure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A majority of the membership' could mean a majority of the full membership or of those present, and Section 14.5(a)'s use of 'majority of the full membership' invites the contrast. That is a nameable ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.3(a) and 13.3(b) require unanimity for particular actions, which qualifies rather than contradicts the majority rule, and 15.1(s)2 presumes federal concurrence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Organisational directives stated definitely; the advisor provision is discretionary but clear. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(r) modifies the uncompensated-advisor premise for the federal advisor, and New York §632 designates a specific advisor; both supplement rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary or convenient to effectuate its powers or duties within the basin' is an open standard, and the last sentence's 'such power' is a loose back-reference. Some genuine looseness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 1.2(e)'s facilities 'within or without the basin' and with Article 9 sales; the consent requirement is a limit that fits, not a clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad mandate language ('develop and effectuate plans, policies and projects') but expressed as a general charter rather than a testable term. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.2, 13.1 and 13.2, which supply the machinery. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory cross-reference to Article 13; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 13 does contain the corresponding duties, though 13.2's 'ensuing six years' differs in specificity from 3.2(b). The introduction itself is consistent.
judgments.clause_name: Section 3.2 Comprehensive Plan, Program and Budgets (introduction)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single duty stated definitely, with 'interested public bodies' the only soft phrase. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates Section 13.1 in substance; 13.1 adds public hearings and utilities, a difference in detail that is easily harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such reasonably foreseeable period as the commission may determine' and 'all public and private projects affecting the basin' are broad, but the drafting is deliberate. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.2 fixes the same program at 'the ensuing six years or such other reasonably foreseeable period', so the two provisions differ in what the default period is.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite budget duty; 'consistent with the water resources program' is a clear enough constraint.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Tracks Section 13.3 exactly. Consistent with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In accordance with the doctrine of equitable apportionment' imports an entire external body of law whose content is contested, and 'as need appears' is vague. That is a nameable interpretive hook.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph (b) then says no allocation 'shall be deemed to constitute an apportionment of the waters of the basin among the parties', which sits uneasily with the equitable-apportionment power just granted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and definite, though 'state of emergency resulting from a drought or catastrophe' and 'such limited time as may be necessary' leave judgment room. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Sections 3.4 and 3.5 and with New York §633's prior-approval requirement; these mesh as designed, with only ordinary friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso preserving power to 'enter into covenants with respect to water supply' after denying any superiority of right is a fine and contestable line. 'Superiority of right' is itself undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The denial that allocations constitute apportionment is hard to square with the Section 3.3 opening grant to allocate 'in accordance with the doctrine of equitable apportionment'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any proper party' is undefined and the split between de novo Supreme Court review for out-of-basin diversions and ordinary review for everything else invites boundary argument. Real vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.4's waiver of rights to seek decree modification and 15.1(p)'s grant of original federal district court jurisdiction both bear on this route to review.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long waiver with two exceptions whose scope ('to effectuate rights, powers, duties and obligations under Section 3.3') is contestable. Moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The waiver and Section 3.3(c)'s preservation of Supreme Court original jurisdiction pull against each other, and New York §633 adds a state consent condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A framing non-impairment clause with 'without limitation thereto' signalling that the list following is illustrative. Mildly open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'except as specifically provided in Sections 3.3 and 3.4' carve-out is the seam where those sections' own exceptions must be fitted; workable but not airtight.
judgments.clause_name: Section 3.5 Supreme Court Decree; Specific Limitations on Commission (introduction)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Impede or interfere with' is an elastic standard applied to a decree's rights and conditions. Some argument available.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with Section 3.3(a)'s emergency power to alter decree diversions, which by definition affects those rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat prohibition on fees for decree-permitted diversions; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.7's broad rate power and Section 15.1(b)'s separate reservation about charges cover overlapping ground, creating a set of limits that must be stacked.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but definite: no jurisdiction over decree-related works absent consent of all decree parties. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies Section 3.8's universal submission requirement, an interaction the drafters flagged in 3.8 itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, entirely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.3(a)'s reference to consulting the river master. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-word introduction; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Article 3 as a whole. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary, convenient or useful for the purposes of this compact' is a wide self-judging standard tacked to a long verb string. Moderate vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is limited by Sections 3.5, 4.5, 7.4(b), 8.2(b) and 9.3, and by 15.1(a)'s requirement of congressional authorisation for projects; the layering is dense but coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Including without limitation thereto' followed by six specific facility types is the classic general-plus-enumeration structure, and the residual reach of 'all projects and facilities ... which affect its water resources' is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same breadth question recurs in Sections 3.8 and 11.2(b); nothing squarely contradicts the standard-setting power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Research power with an illustrative 'including without limitation thereto' list; broad but the catch-all does little operative work here. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.6(e), 6.2(b) and 10.2 investigative powers. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trailing 'or other purposes' is an open catch-all, though the subject matter (forecasting data) is narrow. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Dovetails with Section 6.4 flood warnings. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such special ground water investigations ... as may be required to formulate and administer the comprehensive plan' is bounded by the plan itself. Fairly definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 13.1's plan machinery. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An informational power, plainly expressed. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.12 reports. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such loans, grants, services or other aids as may be lawfully available' is broad but conditioned on lawfulness. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps Sections 12.20(c) and 14.1(a)(2) and 14.13; the overlap is cumulative rather than contradictory, though 15.1(e) qualifies federal funds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure catch-all — 'such other and different powers' plus 'all powers necessary or convenient ... or which may be reasonably implied' — whose reach against the enumerated powers is exactly the ejusdem generis problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Section 14.1(a)(6) and must be reconciled with the express prohibitions in Sections 3.5, 4.5 and 9.3, which an implied-powers reading could swallow.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Without regulation or control by any department, office or agency of any signatory party' is emphatic and definite; the rate categories are broad but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(b) expressly cuts back this power for pre-existing free withdrawals and navigation, and Sections 3.5(b) and 11.3 add further limits — a real set of countervailing provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No project having a substantial effect on the water resources of the basin' turns on two elastic terms — 'project' as defined in 1.2(g) and 'substantial effect' — and the approval standard adds 'substantially impair or conflict with the comprehensive plan'. Multiple nameable ambiguities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its universal reach must be squared with Sections 3.3 and 3.5, with 11.1(b)/11.2(b)'s narrower comprehensive-plan inclusion rules, and with 15.1(a) and 15.1(s), which subordinate projects to congressional and presidential control.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text reads 'To this end, but with limitation thereto, the commission may', where every parallel provision in the compact says 'without limitation thereto' — a mechanical error that reverses the meaning of the following list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Compared with Sections 3.5, 3.6(b), 4.1 and 4.2(a), the omitted 'out' is plainly a slip; nothing else in the compact depends on the mistaken reading.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Advise, consult, contract, financially assist, or otherwise cooperate' — the residual 'otherwise cooperate' is mild and the subject narrow. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 11.5 and 14.1(a)(2). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trailing 'or for any other purpose' is an unbounded catch-all after a specific list of design and construction functions. That is a genuine list-scope point, if a low-stakes one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.5's direction to employ existing agencies. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'So far as consistent with the comprehensive plan' is a workable condition; 'permit the decentralized administration thereof' is loose but discretionary. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Sections 13.1 and 1.5. No conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single definite authorisation to qualify as a sponsoring agency. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.6(g). 15.1(o) limits other federal agencies, not the commission.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive and illustrative in listing possible committee members; no operative uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.6's advisors provision. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Without limitation thereto' plus 'at such off-river sites as it may find appropriate' broadens a specific list, leaving the outer edge of the power uncertain. Moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.5 forbids engaging in 'the business of distributing water', which cuts against the broadest reading of this general water-supply power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumeration of purposes ends with 'and other purposes', an open catch-all after a specific list. Otherwise the grant is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 6.1 and 13.1; paragraph (b) supplies the correlative state duty.
judgments.clause_name: Section 4.2(a) Storage and Release of Waters

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Augmentation of flow to be diminished by the diversion of any water' is awkwardly phrased but the prohibition and its three exceptions are identifiable. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Sections 3.3(a) and 3.5(b), which protect decree diversions, and Article 10 permits; these interlock without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Specially benefited thereby to a measurable extent' and the cap at 'the actual benefit to any water user' are quantitatively vague standards that two parties could apply very differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.5(b) forbids charges on decree-permitted diversions and Section 11.3 reserves state taxing power; both bound this assessment power without contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All existing rights, plans and programs ... which are pertinent' is broad but the duty (review, consider, hold a hearing) is definite. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.4(b) enumerates the occasions requiring hearings and adds 'all other cases wherein this compact requires a public hearing', which absorbs this one; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Engage in the business of distributing water' draws a line between transmission and distribution that is genuinely contestable at the margin. That phrase is the nameable ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts back Section 4.1's broad water-supply power, which authorises transmission and control of use; the boundary between the two is the friction point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain powers to investigate and to build pollution-control works; 'invoke as complainant' is unusual but clear. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.2 to 5.4 and with 15.1(k)'s preservation of federal pollution functions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not injuriously affect waters of the basin' is the operative standard and is markedly vague, as is 'within a time reasonable for the construction of the necessary works'. Named terms available.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5 preserves stricter state law and 15.1(k) preserves federal functions; these coexist with, rather than contradict, the commission's standards.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A covenant framed by highly qualitative criteria — 'satisfactory condition', 'after reasonable treatment', 'free from unsightly or malodorous nuisances' — whose application is inherently contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It obliges states to enact 'any necessary legislation', which sits alongside Section 5.5's reservation of additional state authority; complementary rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed enforcement machinery stated definitely; 'reasonable time for the construction of any necessary works' is the only soft element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Any court of competent jurisdiction' here is narrowed by 15.1(p) and by New York §634, and 15.1(k) preserves federal roles; supplementation, not conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short saving clause; 'additional conditions and restrictions to lessen or prevent' pollution is clear in direction. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It leaves open whether a stricter state rule may frustrate a commission classification under Section 5.2, a tension between state autonomy and the single-agency premise of Section 1.3(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As it may deem necessary or desirable' and 'as the commission may deem appropriate' are self-judging but unmistakable in effect. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.2(a) storage and release powers and Article 13's plan requirement. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Recommended standards' is an odd object for a power to 'adopt, amend and repeal', leaving unclear whether the standards bind anyone. That is a real ambiguity in a single word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.3 requires commission land acquisition to 'be in accord with the standards adopted and promulgated pursuant to Section 6.2', which treats them as operative, while this paragraph disclaims restriction on state and local zoning power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Encroachment lines', 'relative risk of flood' and 'standards for flood plain use which will safeguard the public health, safety and property' are broad but the procedure is definite. Moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with paragraph (a)'s 'recommended standards' label, the effect of standards adopted here on non-consenting municipalities is uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unwarranted constrictions that reduce the ability of the river channel to carry flood water' is an evaluative phrase whose threshold is unstated. Nameable vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties acquisition to Section 6.2 standards, which that section calls merely 'recommended' — a coherence question about whether recommendations can support condemnation under Section 14.14.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive posting and publication powers; 'particularly subject to flood' and 'as conditions may warrant' are soft but harmless. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.6(d) and 6.2(b). No conflict.
judgments.clause_name: Section 6.4 Flood and Stream Stage Warnings and Posting

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall promote sound practices of watershed management' is aspirational but not a term needing definition for any concrete dispute. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 7.2 to 7.4. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain permissive powers over soil conservation and forestry projects. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.4(b) forbids operation where another agency is available, which qualifies the word 'operate' used here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Related to the water resources of the basin' bounds the power; otherwise definite. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same qualification by Section 7.4(b) as the neighbouring powers; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A cooperation duty in general terms; 'appropriate agencies' is the only soft term. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 1.5 and 11.5. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No other suitable unit or agency of government is available to operate the same upon reasonable conditions' packs three vague criteria — suitable, available, reasonable — into a precondition on operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restricts the operating powers granted in Sections 7.2 and 7.3 and invokes Section 1.5, while Section 1.3(c) declares a single agency essential; the pull is real if reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Water related public sports and recreational facilities' is broad but the mandate is clear and expressly subject to Section 8.2. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mandatory 'shall provide for the development' sits against Section 8.2(b)'s bar on operating where another agency is available; harmonisable by distinguishing development from operation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A general cooperation duty, definite in kind. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 7.4(a); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The same triple vagueness as Section 7.4(b): 'suitable', 'available' and 'upon reasonable conditions' govern whether the commission may operate at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restricts Sections 8.1 and 8.3(c), the latter of which expressly contemplates commission operation of recreational facilities and letting of concessions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Within limits prescribed by this article' is a clear internal cross-reference. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 8.2 and 8.4. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Encourage' and 'assist in the coordination' are soft verbs but no dispute would turn on them. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 8.2(a). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A recommendation power, plainly expressed. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallels Section 6.2(a)'s recommended standards; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: administration, operation and maintenance of facilities the commission owns, plus concession letting. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes commission operation, which Section 8.2(b) permits only after a negative finding about other agencies, and Section 15.1(l) removes federally operated facilities from Section 8.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Upon sealed competitive bids after public advertisement therefore' misspells 'therefor', but the requirement is unmistakable. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(l) expressly disapplies this section to facilities operated under other federal law, a carve-out that must be tracked.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'May be impounded and used by or under authority of the commission ... in accordance with the comprehensive plan' is definite in structure. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.5 protects decree diversions and 15.1(s) allows presidential suspension of plan provisions; both qualify without contradicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain power to develop and operate, or authorise, generating dams. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 9.1 and 9.4 and with Section 2.7's authority to dispose of hydroelectric power outside the basin.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The business of direct sale to consumers' is a boundary phrase that could be argued at the margin, as is 'not otherwise available upon reasonable terms'. Moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.7 permits the commission 'to sell or dispose of ... hydroelectric power' generally, so the wholesale-only limit here must be read into that broader language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'On reasonable terms, consideration and duration' is a soft standard but familiar and bounded by notice and hearing. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 9.2 and 14.4(b) hearings. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable, nondiscriminatory, and just' is a classic triad of open-textured rate standards whose application is contestable, though the concepts are well worn in utility law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.7 lets the commission fix rates 'without regulation or control by any department, office or agency of any signatory party', which leaves no obvious body to apply this standard.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such powers of the commission as it may deem necessary or desirable' to delegate is broad but plainly discretionary. The sentence also reads 'such power or regulation or control', an apparent slip for 'of'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: New York §637 forbids state agencies from accepting delegations they could not otherwise exercise, a limit imposed from Part II on this power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Have developed or threaten to develop to such a degree as to create a water shortage' is a predictive and undefined threshold. Nameable vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 10.3 to 10.6, which build on the designation. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grandfather clause for permits 'heretofore granted under the laws of any of the signatory states' is definite in words but its temporal reference ('heretofore' relative to what) is loose. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.8 provides that state permits 'shall be superseded to the extent of any conflict' with commission regulation, which is difficult to reconcile with the exemption preserved here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Drought or other condition which may cause an actual and immediate shortage' pairs a specific with an open catch-all, though 'actual and immediate' tightens it. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with Section 3.3(a)'s separate emergency mechanism requiring unanimity and consultation with the river master; the two emergency powers overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The just and equitable interests and rights of other lawful users' and 'water of the quality required' are evaluative standards with no metric. Real vagueness in a permitting criterion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 10.3 and 10.4 and reviewable under 10.6. No square conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any court of competent jurisdiction' is undefined in the compact, though the cross-references to 10.2 through 10.5 are precise. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: New York §634 defines the phrase for that state and 15.1(p) gives federal district courts original jurisdiction; the forum question is answered outside this section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A recordkeeping duty in definite terms, contents left to commission prescription. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 10.3 and 14.11. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Whenever the commission finds it necessary or desirable' plus supersession 'to the extent of any conflict' is broad but its operation is clear. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is hard to square with Section 10.3(ii), which preserves withdrawals made pursuant to previously granted state permits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A framing sentence with a definite purpose statement and cross-reference to Section 1.4. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'subject in each case to Section 1.4' proviso, plus 15.1(s), materially qualifies what follows; the framing itself is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All projects related to powers delegated to the commission' is broad but the duty is only consultation. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 11.1(c) and with 15.1(s)'s preservation of federal authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Nor shall it be deemed authorized' is a strong bar whose reference — expenditure, commitment or authorisation of any federal project — is sweeping. Moderate-low as drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is difficult to reconcile with 11.1(c)'s preservation of existing federal agency authority and with 15.1(s)1, which subordinates the plan to constitutional federal authority and presidential suspension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as specifically provided by this section' is a clear pointer, though what counts as 'specifically provided' is arguable. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph (b)'s absolute bar on unlisted federal projects and this preservation of agency authority pull in opposite directions, a tension 15.1(s) attempts to manage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A framing sentence, definite in expression. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the parallel Section 11.1 introduction. No conflict.
judgments.clause_name: Section 11.2 State and Local Agencies and Projects (introduction)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Consultation duty in broad but workable terms. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 11.2(c) and Section 1.5. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: On its face no state or local expenditure on 'any project or facility' may be made unless first included in the comprehensive plan — an absolute rule with no materiality threshold. The breadth of 'any project or facility' is the pressure point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.8 conditions review on a 'substantial effect on the water resources of the basin' and 11.2(c) preserves state agency authority, so the three provisions cannot all be read at full strength.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as specifically provided by this section' is a definite carve-out phrase whose scope depends on paragraph (b). Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Preserving all pre-existing state authority sits awkwardly beside paragraph (b)'s blanket prohibition on unplanned expenditure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short reservation of taxing power, definite in wording; 'measured by the withdrawal or diversion' is precise enough. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It stands against Sections 3.7 and 4.3 (commission charges and assessments) and Section 3.5(b), and 15.1(b) adds a further layer about charges.
judgments.clause_name: Section 11.3 Reserved Taxing Powers of States

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Uniform standards', 'equitable cost sharing and reimbursement formulas' are open-ended aims but the duty to establish them is clear. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.20(a) and 13.3(b), which depend on these formulas. No conflict.
judgments.clause_name: Section 11.4 Project Costs and Evaluation Standards (introduction)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, technical item in a list of required procedures. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 13.3(b)'s per-project cost allocation. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Descriptive of contracts and arrangements to be developed; no ambiguous operative term. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.20(a) and 14.13. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An accounting-system item, definite. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.11 audit provisions. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Payments in lieu of taxes' is a defined concept elsewhere in the compact; the item is clear. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mutual pledge qualified by 'within the limits of available appropriations' and by 'whenever the parties deem appropriate' for reimbursement, which makes the obligation nearly unenforceable. Moderate vagueness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Bonds are said to be 'payable solely out of the properties and revenues of the commission without recourse to taxation' and yet to be 'direct and general obligations' with 'full faith and credit of the commission' pledged — an internal pull between limited and general obligation language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening sentence — 'The purpose of this compact shall include without limitation thereto all costs of any project' — is grammatically garbled; 'purpose' plainly should be the purposes for which bonds may be issued, and as written it says something different.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Section 12.1's 'any of the purposes of this compact', the intent is recoverable, so the defect is textual rather than a clash with another provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two flat prohibitions, definite in scope. Nothing ambiguous named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.20(b) permits bonds to be sold 'with or without the guaranty of such signatory party', which qualifies the no-pledge rule stated here.
judgments.clause_name: Section 12.3 Credit Excluded; Officers, State and Municipal

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Technical refunding provisions expressed definitely; 'whenever the commission deems it expedient' is discretionary but clear. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.5, 12.6 and 12.13. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but conventional bond-authorisation provision with definite mechanics. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.6, 12.13 and 12.18; 15.1(a) adds a congressional authorisation precondition for projects, not for bond mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very long, but each element is specified; the phrase 'other than any restriction on the regulatory powers vested in the commission' is a clear carve-out. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That carve-out coordinates with the commission's regulatory powers in Articles 3, 5 and 10, and the pledge language matches Section 12.18. Consistent.
judgments.clause_name: Section 12.6 Bonds; Resolutions and Indentures Generally

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No bond or its terms shall mature in more than fifty years from its own date' is oddly phrased ('or its terms') but the fifty-year cap is unmistakable. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A place-of-payment permission, plainly worded. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 12.6. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Execution and signature-survival rules are standard and definite. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 12.3's bar on personal liability. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, definite. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.4 and 12.18. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short negotiability rule with a clear exception for registered bonds. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.5 and 12.6 on registration. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite legal-investment declaration. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recording and pledge-effectiveness rules stated definitely. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.6 and 12.18. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 3.2(b) and feeds Sections 11.1(b)/11.2(b)'s inclusion requirement; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single definite content requirement. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 3.2(b). Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but plainly worded receipt-and-reimbursement power. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite planning and specification power. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite control power over its own facilities. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.14 and 14.15 on acquisition and conveyance. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introductory clause. Nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.5 and 14.5(a). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One short, definite power. Nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-word introduction. Nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One flat sentence: all meetings open to the public. Definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite, with amount left to the commission. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short bribery prohibition in definite terms. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.14(a)'s exclusion of signatory property from condemnation, which this voluntary-conveyance route complements.
judgments.clause_name: Section 14.15(a) Conveyance of Lands and Relocation of Public Facilities

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Notwithstanding any contrary provision of law' is emphatic but 'authorized and empowered ... to grant and convey' remains permissive despite 'upon the commission's request'. A slight tension in a single sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with paragraph (a) and Section 14.14(a), which reaches political subdivision property by condemnation if needed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not in any event exceed the expenditure required to serve the public convenience and necessity' imports an undefined utility-law standard as a cost cap. Nameable vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.14(a)'s treatment of public utility facilities and with Article 11 cost allocation. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subject to such reasonable conditions as the highway department of the signatory party may require' leaves the conditions open but the grant is definite. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.15(c) on relocation of highways. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The default penalty applies 'in the absence of such provision' by a signatory state, a conditional trigger that is workable but fact-dependent; 'attempts or conspires' is definite. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.4 and 14.2(a) enforcement provisions and with 14.8(d). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Liability is fixed 'only to the extent and subject to the procedures prescribed by law generally with respect to officers, agents and employees of the government of the United States', an incorporation by reference whose content is external but identifiable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(m) provides that for the Federal Tort Claims Act statutes the commission 'shall not be considered a Federal agency', which makes the incorporated federal regime awkward to apply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad non-interference clause; 'affecting or intending to affect or in any way to interfere with' is emphatic but its object (riparian rights law) is identifiable. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.14(a) authorises condemnation of riparian rights and Article 10 regulates withdrawals, both of which plainly affect riparian law — a real internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'May be adopted by legislative action of any of the signatory parties concurred in by all of the others' is clear, though 'to implement the purposes thereof' is a soft limit on what may be amended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(q) reserves Congress's unilateral right to alter, amend or repeal its consenting Act, which cuts against the unanimity requirement stated here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonably and liberally construed' is a construction directive whose pull is itself contestable, and severability is stated definitely. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A liberal-construction instruction sits against the express limitations in Sections 3.5, 4.5, 9.3 and 11.3, and is exactly the sort of provision invoked to widen the contested definitions in Section 1.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Thirty days after the enactment of concurring legislation' and the execution formalities are definite. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: New York §2 refers to 'subdivision twenty-one of section fourteen of article fourteen' as the effective-date and execution provision, but that is Section 14.21 (severability), not 14.22 — a mismatched cross-reference from Part II.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A framing sentence tying the reservations to Section 1.4; definite. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.4's express recognition of congressional power, and the reservations that follow are the operative material.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is OCR-corrupted ('untilC', 'includingC') and the exception for 'a project for which State supplied funds only will be used' is a significant undefined boundary. Moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Requiring an Act of Congress before any project proceeds beyond planning is hard to reconcile with Article 12's bond powers, Section 3.6(a) and Section 13.1's plan machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It forbids the commission 'to impose any change for water withdrawals or diversions', where 'change' is plainly a mechanical error for 'charge' — a mistake that alters the sentence's meaning as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restricts Section 3.7's rate power and overlaps Section 3.5(b), and the closing proviso makes the paragraph applicable only 'to the extent not inconsistent with Section 1.4', a circularity that complicates the fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The executive powers of the President in the event of a national emergency' is broad and undefined, but the clause is a saving provision. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Sections 3.3(a) and 10.4 emergency mechanisms and with 15.1(s)'s presidential suspension power. No square conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall serve at the pleasure of the President' is definite in itself; the marginal footnote records its repeal. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The compact's own endnote states that this section and Section 2.2 'were inconsistent as to the term of the federal representative's appointment' — an acknowledged internal conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is convoluted ('impairing or in any manner affecting the applicability to all Federal funds ... or such authority') and its object is grammatically incomplete. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies Section 13.3(c)'s budget covenant and Section 12.20(a) as to federal contributions; consistent in substance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Are or may continued to be free or exempt' contains a mechanical error ('may continued'), and the double-negative structure of the whole sentence is hard to parse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly cuts back Section 12.8, which exempts the bonds from 'all taxation by or under authority of any of the signatory parties' — a defined term that includes the federal government.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Legally or morally' is unusual but the disclaimer is unambiguous. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.1 and 12.3; 12.20(b)'s optional guarantee is a separate voluntary undertaking.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in effect: services pledged only as agencies agree or the President directs. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly displaces Section 11.5's pledge of technical and administrative services, an override the drafters flagged with 'notwithstanding'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but highly specific, incorporating named statutes and a defined overtime rule; the internal citation punctuation is imperfect but the substance is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies to projects 'undertaken by the commission or ... financially assisted by it', which sits alongside Sections 14.9 and 15.1(j) without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite dollar threshold and a named statute. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.9's own $10,000 construction threshold and $2,500 supply threshold; complementary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause preserves federal pollution functions but then provides that their exercise 'shall not limit the authority of the commission', which is close to self-contradictory as a priority rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Sections 5.2 to 5.5 it leaves unresolved which authority prevails in an actual clash between a federal standard and a commission regulation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Facilities operated pursuant to any other Federal law' is a broad but identifiable category. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carves federal facilities out of Section 8.4's competitive concession requirement, an express and workable exception.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of specific statutes followed by a flat declaration; the enumeration is closed, which reduces catch-all risk. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.18 measures the commission's tort liability by the law governing United States officers and employees, which is awkward once the commission is declared not a federal agency for the FTCA statutes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long parenthetical exclusion but each category is identified; 'solely and directly' is the only soft phrase. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.5, 14.8(d) and 15.1(m). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not be deemed to enlarge the authority of any Federal agency other than the commission' is a definite negative. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits beside 11.1(c)'s preservation of existing federal authority and 15.1(s)'s reservations; complementary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite grant of original federal jurisdiction with a removal mechanism and an immunity reservation. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The compact repeatedly channels review to 'any court of competent jurisdiction' (Sections 3.8, 4.3, 5.4, 10.6) and New York §634 defines that phrase as the state supreme court, which is difficult to square with exclusive federal original jurisdiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two reservations of congressional power, plainly stated. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The unilateral right to alter or repeal cuts against Section 14.20's requirement of unanimous concurrence for amendments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At the rates which he shall deem to prevail in respect to comparable officers' is discretionary but clear. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly overrides Sections 2.4 and 2.6's uncompensated-service rule for the federal member and advisor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence with two nested provisos, a typo ('United Sates'), and the elastic standards 'shall not substantially conflict' and 'whenever the President shall find ... that the national interest so requires'. Substantial internal complexity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It subordinates the comprehensive plan and Sections 3.8 and 11.1 to federal authority and permits unilateral presidential deletion of plan provisions, which is hard to reconcile with Section 13.1's plan-adoption scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The withdrawal window — 'between the first and sixtieth day of the sixth year after the initial adoption ... and of every sixth year thereafter' — is a precise but easily miscounted formula. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies the concurrence mechanism assumed by paragraph 1 and interacts with Section 13.1's power to revise the plan at any time; the two timelines do not obviously align.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Automatic federal withdrawal 'except to the extent that the President deems remaining a party necessary and proper' is an odd partial-exit standard that is hard to apply. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Sections 1.4, 1.6 and 14.21's severability rule, which says invalidity 'shall not be affected thereby' — a different consequence for the same event.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A sweeping implied-amendment clause ('All Acts or parts of Acts inconsistent ... are hereby amended') paired with a proviso that no commission act may repeal, modify or amend any federal law — the two halves pull against each other.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 15.1(k), (o) and (s), which preserve other federal statutory functions; the combined effect on conflicts is unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such action as may be necessary and proper, in his discretion' is broad but this is an enabling effectuation clause. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the Delaware, New Jersey and Pennsylvania effectuation sections. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall cooperate with and furnish appropriate assistance' followed by 'may include the detailing of personnel' mixes mandatory and permissive terms; 'appropriate' is undefined. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(h) pledges federal services only as agencies agree or the President directs, which is a narrower commitment than the 'shall cooperate' language here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Effect Date' in the heading is a typo for 'Effective Date', and the operative sentence is definite. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'This Act shall take effect immediately' concerns the consenting Act, whereas Section 14.22 makes the compact binding thirty days after all concurring legislation — a distinction that must be drawn to avoid conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A general repealer of 'all acts and parts of acts inconsistent' — inherently indeterminate as to what is repealed, though that is the standard form. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the New Jersey, New York and Pennsylvania repealers; New York §641 states the same idea differently. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short discretionary effectuation authority. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the other states' effectuation sections and 15.2(a). Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, definite. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Immediate effect of the state act must be reconciled with Section 14.22's thirty-day rule for the compact itself; the distinction between act and compact resolves it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A general repealer whose scope depends on identifying inconsistent laws; standard but indeterminate. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the Delaware and Pennsylvania repealers. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite discretionary authority. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the other effectuation sections. Consistent.
judgments.clause_name: New Jersey § 15.2 Effectuation by Chief Executive

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One definite sentence. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same act-versus-compact timing point as against Section 14.22; resolvable but present.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence refers to 'the alternate of said department head on the water resources commission', but no department head has been identified — a broken antecedent that obscures who acts in the governor's absence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its cross-references to 'the second' and 'third subdivision of section two of article two' track Sections 2.2 and 2.3 correctly, but the reimbursement rule differs in mechanism from Section 2.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The designation and notice mechanics for the mayor's designee are definite. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'subdivision six of section two of article two', which is Section 2.6's advisor provision — an accurate cross-reference; the second paragraph adds a state advisory committee not contemplated by Section 3.10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The state consent condition is definite; the reference to 'section four hundred fifty-two of the conservation law' is external but specific. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It correctly points to Section 3.3(a)'s unanimous-consent requirement and imposes an internal state precondition on giving that consent; consistent in operation.
judgments.clause_name: New York § 633. Consent to Alteration of Diversions

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines 'court of competent jurisdiction' three ways for three different compact provisions, which is careful drafting, though the citation to the 'civil practice act' is dated. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(p) gives United States district courts original jurisdiction over cases arising under the compact, which cuts against these state-court designations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite prohibition on state permits where commission approval is required and absent. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends entirely on Section 3.8's contested threshold for what requires commission approval, so its reach is only as clear as that provision.
judgments.clause_name: New York § 635. Prior to Project Approval

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enabling power for municipalities, plainly worded. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its cross-reference to 'paragraph (b) of subdivision two of section six of article six' correctly identifies Section 6.2(b)'s aid agreements. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite limitation keyed to the state agency's own constitutional or statutory power. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restricts the delegation power the commission is given by Section 10.1, a limit imposed unilaterally by one signatory's implementing act.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite, mirroring the compact's cooperative-services language. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Tracks Section 11.5 including the 'available appropriations' limit. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The ensuring fiscal year' is a typo for 'ensuing', and the provision requires the commission itself to submit estimates to a state budget director. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.3(b)(2) requires transmittal of certified budget copies to each party's principal budget officer, so this adds a state-specific procedure that must be squared with the compact's apportionment mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite audit authority with a clear reporting line. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its cross-reference to 'paragraph (b) of subdivision eleven of section fourteen of article fourteen' correctly identifies Section 14.11(b). Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No provision of ... any other law, which is inconsistent' leaves the identification of inconsistency open, the usual indeterminacy of such clauses. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the other states' repealers and Section 15.1(u)'s federal analogue. Consistent in function.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It twice invokes 'subdivision twenty-one of section fourteen of article fourteen' as the effective-date and execution provision, but Section 14.21 is Construction and Severability while 14.22 is the effective-date section — a mechanical cross-reference error in an operative direction to the Governor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Section 14.22, which actually prescribes signing, sealing and filing in six duplicate originals, the mis-citation must be corrected by construction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One definite sentence. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its immediate effect is qualified by §2's incorporation of the compact's own thirty-day rule in Section 14.22; harmonisable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A general repealer of inconsistent acts; standard but indeterminate in reach. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the Delaware and New Jersey repealers. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite discretionary authority. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the other effectuation sections and 15.2(a). Consistent.
judgments.clause_name: Pennsylvania Section 3. Effectuation by Chief Executive

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One definite sentence. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same act-versus-compact effective-date distinction against Section 14.22. Resolvable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is an editorial endnote rather than an operative term; it quotes statutes accurately and includes ellipses and asterisks that make its quoted text incomplete. Little to construe as a promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly records that Sections 2.2 and 15.1(d) 'were inconsistent as to the term of the federal representative's appointment' and that later statutes displaced the printed text of Section 2.2 — an acknowledged mismatch between the printed compact and current law.
judgments.clause_name: Endnote 1,4 (1997 Act and WRDA amendments to Sections 2.2 and 15.1(d))

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An explanatory endnote quoting amended federal appropriation directives; 'equitable funding requirements' is vague but is the statute's own phrase. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on Section 13.3(c)'s covenant to include apportioned amounts and on Section 12.20(a), indicating that the federal funding obligation is governed by statute rather than by the compact text alone.
